summary: mymatasan can now export footage as a verifiable evidence bundle. Ask for a time range on a camera, state a reason, and get a single .zip containing the joined video, a manifest.json recording where it came from and what it covers, and a plain-text VERIFY.txt explaining how to check it with standard tools. Until now playback and download worked per stored segment only, so producing '14:05 to 14:40 on camera 3' meant downloading several files and stitching them externally — which destroys any claim the footage is unmodified and left no record that it happened. Segments are now SHA-256 hashed at finalize, on the plaintext mp4 before at-rest encryption, so the digest survives a key change, a backup and restore, and a move between hosts. That is what lets a bundle claim the footage was not altered between recording and export; a segment with no stored digest (recorded before this existed, or recovered after a crash when the file was already encrypted) is hashed at export time and labelled 'computed-at-export' instead, because that only proves the file has not changed since the export and must not be presented as the stronger claim. The manifest always lists every gap in the requested range — an export that silently skips missing footage looks continuous, which is worse than refusing to export — and the export dialog shows those gaps before the operator commits. A segment whose stored digest does not match the bytes on disk fails the export rather than being included quietly. Exporting is grantable to operators as a new second level on the Recordings page; deleting footage remains superadmin-only, which is the same line drawn twice: an operator who was present at an incident must be able to hand the footage to somebody and must not be able to destroy it. Every export is audited at both request and download.
compatibility: Backward compatible, additive. recording_segment gains a sha256 column (added by the auto-migrator; existing rows stay blank and are reported honestly as unhashed). New endpoints under /api/evidence. The Recordings page gains a 'use' level granting export — the built-in operator role now holds it, matching the policy matrix. Bundles are written under <dataDir>/exports and removed after 6 hours. Not yet live-benched: the acceptance test is to export a range spanning a gap and verify the output digest, the source digests and the listed gap.
